judge_input.description:
Closes #11441

### Adds OCI-Friendly Chunked Encoding Toggle for Nessie Catalog S3 Clients
What this particular PR does is go ahead and take the behavior of the catalog's own S3 client and turn it into something that is now fully configurable, and the reason for doing that is so that any deployments which happen to be specifically targeting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (and, along with that, any of the other various S3-compatible services that are out there which end up rejecting the chunked payload signatures) are thereby able to go and disable the chunked transfer encoding, doing so in a complete end-to-end sort of fashion. The option that does this is one that is exposed right out at the level of the configuration API itself, and from there it is then propagated onward and through the catalog implementation, and beyond that it is also properly documented over within Helm, and then on top of all of that it is additionally covered by a whole set of tests as well.

**Key changes:**

- Introduces the chunked-encoding-enabled setting, placing it onto S3BucketOptions, along with a whole number of accompanying helpers that go with it, and then goes on from there to wire that particular setting into S3ClientSupplier, and it does this in such a way and to such a degree that the per-bucket overrides that get specified are genuinely and fully able to make their way all the way through and finally reach the AWS SDK S3Configuration at the end of it all.
- Extends the Helm chart (and by that is meant specifically the values.yaml file itself, the README, the various helpers, and also the templates that are within it) as well as, on top of that, the Quarkus sample config, and it goes about doing all of this in such a way that both the global defaults on the one hand and also the per-bucket settings on the other hand are each of them able, independently, to go and toggle the chunked encoding on or off.
- Adds in some dedicated unit coverage (over in the TestS3ClientSupplier class) which goes on to properly verify both the default AWS behavior on the one hand and also, on the other hand, the explicit true and the explicit false values that are able to be set, and this is precisely the kind of thing that goes a very long way indeed toward preventing any future regressions from ever creeping their way back in later on.
- Updates the changelog so as to properly highlight and call attention to the brand new configuration hook that has been added in as part of this whole piece of work here.

**Testing:**

`./gradlew :nessie-catalog-files-impl:test --tests org.projectnessie.catalog.files.s3.TestS3ClientSupplier`
judge_input.title: Add OCI friendly S3 chunked encoding toggle
